<!--
HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE
- Copy the whole claims/_template/ folder to claims/<claim-id>/.
- Structured fields (verdicts, certainty scores, reviewers, registration, changelog) live in
  claim.yml. The study table lives in studies.csv. The R chunks below render them. Do NOT
  retype any of that content into prose.
- Prose sections are written here. Every empirical sentence cites a studies.csv row by its
  study_id in brackets, e.g. [S03], plus a bibliography key [@key].
- Keep every section heading, in this order. A section with nothing to say keeps its heading
  and one sentence explaining why.
- Delete these instructions and all ALL-CAPS placeholders before opening a PR.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(yaml)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
claim   <- read_yaml("claim.yml")
# All columns as text: "[VERIFY]" and empty CSVs would otherwise change column types.
studies <- read_csv("studies.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0) b else a
# Escape brackets that break markdown link text (kable already escapes "|").
md_text <- function(x) gsub("([][])", "\\\\\\1", x %||% "")
# Link only when the target is a real URL; "[VERIFY]" or a placeholder renders as plain text.
md_link <- function(text, url) {
  url <- url %||% ""
  ifelse(grepl("^https?://\\S+$", url) & !grepl("[", url, fixed = TRUE),
         paste0("[", text, "](", url, ")"), text)
}
```

```{r header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("**Claim %s** · Topic: %s · Election relevance: %s · Protocol %s · Last updated %s\n\n",
            claim$id, claim$topic, claim$election_relevance,
            claim$protocol_version, claim$last_updated))
cat("**Where you hear it:** ", claim$public_claim$where_heard, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r verdicts, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# One callout per verdict. Most claims have one; a split claim (shared evidence base,
# two causal statements) has two. See protocol §3.4.
# "Cannot be graded" verdicts carry no certainty grade (protocol §10).
for (v in claim$verdicts) {
  certainty <- if (is.null(v$certainty)) ""
               else sprintf("*Certainty: **%s**.* %s", v$certainty, v$certainty_note %||% "")
  cat(sprintf('::: {.callout-important title="Our assessment — %s: %s"}\n%s\n\n%s\n:::\n\n',
              v$scope, v$verdict, v$statement %||% "", certainty))
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**The 30-second version.** FOUR TO SIX SENTENCES A READER CAN TAKE AWAY IF THEY READ NOTHING ELSE. State what the best evidence is, what it found, where the real disagreement is, and what is still open.
:::

```{r tested, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("::: {.callout-tip collapse=\"true\" title=\"The statement we tested, and how we got there from the public claim\"}\n")
for (t in claim$tested_statements) {
  cat(sprintf("**%s.** %s\n\n", t$scope, t$pecos))
}
cat(claim$public_claim$mapping_note, "\n")
cat(":::\n\n")
```

## Key numbers

```{r keynumbers, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Each number links to its study_id in the table. Figures are the reviewers' summary of
# the table, not new estimates.
for (k in claim$key_numbers) {
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** — %s *(%s)*\n", k$figure, k$label, k$source_rows))
}
```

## 1. What is the policy trying to address?

DESCRIBE THE POLICY IN NEUTRAL TERMS and the distinct goals offered for it. Say which goal this page tests and which belong to other claim pages. Separate any bundled causal statements here (protocol §3.4).

Related claims: LINK EACH RELATED CLAIM PAGE WITH ITS CURRENT VERDICT AND CERTAINTY.

## 2. What does economic theory say?

PLAIN-LANGUAGE ACCOUNT OF THE MECHANISM.

- **Hypothesized effect.** WHAT THEORY PREDICTS, AND WHAT THE SIGN DEPENDS ON.
- **Trade-offs.** WHO BEARS COSTS, THROUGH WHAT CHANNEL. Even if the claim fails, the policy may serve other goals; say so without grading them.
- **Unintended consequences.** BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES THEORY PREDICTS.

Theory says what to look for, not the magnitude. Say so.

## 3. What does the empirical literature say?

TWO OR THREE SENTENCES on why this literature exists in the form it does (which natural experiments, which data), and that every row below has a causal design; descriptive and opinion pieces were screened out (see Methods).

```{r studytable, echo=FALSE}
studies |>
  mutate(Weight = paste0(quality_tier, ifelse(pub_status == "Working paper", "*", ""),
                         " / R", relevance_tier)) |>
  transmute(ID = study_id,
            Study = md_link(md_text(citation), doi_or_url),
            Design = design,
            Setting = paste(country, period, sep = ", "),
            Outcome = md_text(outcome),
            Finding = md_text(finding_summary),
            Weight) |>
  kable(caption = "Included studies. Weight = quality tier A–D / relevance tier 1–3; * = working paper at time of review. Full extraction fields, effect sizes, and standard errors are in the downloadable CSV.")
```

[Download the full study table (CSV)](studies.csv) · [Search log](search-log.csv) · [Full-text exclusions with reasons](screening.csv)

STRUCTURED NARRATIVE SYNTHESIS, in this order (protocol §9.2): direction → magnitude → heterogeneity → mechanism → gaps. Cite rows by ID.

## 4. What can we conclude, and how sure are we?

ONE PARAGRAPH per verdict restating it and naming which criteria hold the certainty grade where it is.

```{r certainty, echo=FALSE}
field <- function(rows, k) vapply(rows, function(r) as.character(r[[k]] %||% ""), character(1))
cs <- claim$certainty_scores
tibble(Scope = field(cs, "scope"), Criterion = field(cs, "criterion"),
       Score = field(cs, "score"), Why = md_text(field(cs, "reason"))) |>
  kable(caption = "Certainty criteria (protocol §11). Scored independently by two reviewers; disagreements noted in the Why column.")
```

```{r rationales, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("::: {.callout-tip collapse=\"true\" title=\"Reviewer rationales\"}\n")
for (r in claim$reviewers) {
  if (nzchar(r$rationale %||% ""))   # the adversarial reader's comment is optional
    cat(sprintf("**%s (%s)** — %s\n\n", r$name %||% "", r$role %||% "", r$rationale))
}
cat(":::\n\n")
```

## 5. What is still unknown?

- OPEN QUESTION, with one sentence on why it is open (no studies, weak designs, no transfer to current setting, horizon too short).
- OPEN QUESTION.

Distinguish "probably small" (a finding) from "unknown" (absence of evidence).

## 6. Where do experts disagree, and why?

CLASSIFY each live dispute as **data**, **method**, **time horizon**, **scope**, or **values** (protocol §12.1), and say what it is *not* about.

**Steelman: “PUBLIC CLAIM”.** THE STRONGEST REASONABLE CASE AGAINST OUR VERDICT, 150–300 words, citing the best opposing evidence by row ID. Checked by: NAME OF ADVERSARIAL READER.

**What would change our assessment.** A FALSIFIABLE STATEMENT: the number and kind of studies, findings, and designs that would move the verdict or the certainty grade.

Expert perspectives (signed, opinion, written after this review): LINKS OR "None yet."

## Methods for this page

```{r methods, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
m <- claim$methods
cat("::: {.callout-tip collapse=\"true\" title=\"Protocol, registration, search, screening, AI use, reviewers\"}\n")
cat(sprintf("- **Protocol:** %s ([read the protocol](../../methods.qmd))\n", claim$protocol_version))
cat(sprintf("- **Registration:** %s, posted %s; amendments: %s\n",
            md_link(m$registration$registry %||% "", m$registration$url),
            m$registration$date %||% "", m$registration$amendments %||% "none"))
cat(sprintf("- **Sources searched:** %s; last run %s; rerun %s\n",
            paste(m$search$sources, collapse = ", "), m$search$last_run %||% "",
            m$search$rerun_schedule %||% ""))
n <- function(x) as.integer(x %||% NA)
cat(sprintf("- **Screening:** %d records → %d after de-duplication → %d full texts → %d included\n",
            n(m$screening$records), n(m$screening$deduplicated),
            n(m$screening$full_text), n(m$screening$included)))
cat(sprintf("- **AI use:** %s\n", m$ai_use %||% ""))
for (r in claim$reviewers) cat(sprintf("- **%s:** %s, %s; conflicts of interest: %s\n",
                                       r$role %||% "", r$name %||% "",
                                       r$affiliation %||% "", r$coi %||% ""))
cat(sprintf("- **Challenge this page / suggest a missing study:** %s\n", m$challenge_contact %||% ""))
cat(":::\n\n")
```

## Changelog

```{r changelog, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (e in rev(claim$changelog)) cat(sprintf("- **%s** (v%s) — %s\n",
                                            e$date %||% "", e$version %||% "", e$note %||% ""))
```
